Matrices of the multilayer assembly model

Source: R/metaWebNetAssemblyML.R
build_multilayer_assembly.Rd

Translates a multilayer network and the parameters beta into the three matrices used by metaWebNetAssemblyMLCT(): the trophic meta-web metaW, the matrix M of effects on the log extinction rate, and the obligate dependence matrix Dep. It is called by metaWebNetAssemblyML(); use it directly to check how the layers were translated.

Usage

build_multilayer_assembly(
  mg,
  layers = default_layer_signs(),
  beta = c(pos = 0, neg = 0),
  layer_beta = NULL,
  obligate_on = NULL,
  type_attr = "type",
  effect_attr = "effect",
  obligate_layers = NULL,
  normalize = TRUE
)

Arguments

mg

the multilayer network: an mgraph (the list of igraph layers returned by multiweb::readMultiplex()) or any list of igraph layers, where the layer id is the list name or, if the list has no names, the type_attr edge attribute; a single igraph with the layer id in the edge attribute type_attr; or a data.frame with columns from, to, layer and, optionally, the sign column effect_attr. Vertices need a name attribute.

layers

data.frame with one row per layer: layer (the id), sign_from, sign_to and rule ("trophic" or "modifier"); see default_layer_signs(). Every layer of mg must be in it, and exactly one must have rule == "trophic".

beta

named numeric vector c(pos = , neg = ): strength of the positive and of the negative effects on the log extinction rate. With normalize = TRUE, exp(beta) is the largest factor by which the partners can change the extinction rate.

layer_beta

optional named numeric vector, a multiplier of beta for each layer (default 1).

obligate_on

character vector of species on which others can depend obligately (e.g. foundation species), or NULL (default) for no obligate dependence.

type_attr

name of the edge attribute with the layer id.

effect_attr

name of the edge attribute (or data.frame column) with the sign of the effect of from on to. If it is NULL or missing, the layer signs are used.

obligate_layers

layers whose positive effects create obligate dependence; NULL (default) uses all modifier layers.

normalize

if TRUE (default) the positive and negative effects on each species are divided by its number of positive and negative partners, so that the effect depends on the fraction of partners present. With FALSE the effects add up per partner present, and a species with many mutualists can become practically immortal.

Value

a list with metaW (logical, metaW[j, i] is TRUE if j is a prey of i), M (numeric), Dep (logical), all with the species as dimnames, and species.

Details

Signs of the links. Each modifier link gives the sign (+1, 0 or -1) of the effect that each of the two species receives from the other. The signs are taken from one of two sources:

  • a sign attribute per link (effect_attr, values "+", "-" or numbers): the link a -> b is the effect of a on b only; an effect of b on a must be another link b -> a. A layer must have the attribute in all its links or in none.

  • otherwise, the signs of the layer in layers: in a link a -> b, a receives sign_from and b receives sign_to.

From signs to M. M[i, j] is the effect of the presence of j on the log extinction rate of i. A positive effect of j on i adds -beta["pos"] to M[i, j] and a negative one adds +beta["neg"], both multiplied by layer_beta[layer] if given. Pairs linked in several layers add their effects. In symmetric layers (sign_from == sign_to) each pair counts once, however many directions are recorded. With normalize = TRUE the negative and positive entries of each row are then divided by the number of partners of that sign.

Obligate dependence. With obligate_on, Dep[i, j] is TRUE if j is in obligate_on, i is not, and j has a positive effect on i in one of obligate_layers.

Self-loops are kept in the trophic layer (cannibals are their own prey) and dropped in the modifier layers.

See also
